$comment: 🧊️ The one committed geometry every 🚪️io round-trip test is driven from: an axis-aligned unit cube on [0,1]³ with 8 shared vertices and 12 triangles, wound counter-clockwise when seen from outside so its signed volume is +1. Chosen because every quantity a mesh format can lose is independently checkable on it — triangle count (12), vertex count (8), bounding box ([0,0,0]..[1,1,1]) and enclosed volume (1.0) — and because 1.0 is exact in binary floating point, so no format's f32 storage introduces a tolerance of its own. Laid out exactly as the renderer's own MeshData wire form (flat f32 triples, u32 index buffer), which is what crosses the mesh bridge.
